content.title: About
content.content: Beans and rice is a popular fast‑food dish consisting of cooked beans (often black beans, pinto beans or chickpeas) mixed with boiled rice. It is usually served in a disposable container, sometimes topped with sauce, cheese or spices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beans and rice are a staple in many Mexican and Latin American fast‑food chains.
The combination provides a complete protein because the amino acid profiles of beans and rice complement each other.
The dish can be easily adapted for vegetarians and vegans by omitting any meat additives.
In some regions it is served with tortilla chips or guacamole for extra flavor.
Traditionally the rice is fluffy and the beans are soft but not mushy.

items.title: Rich source of plant protein
items.content: Beans deliver a substantial amount of protein, and when paired with rice they form a complete amino acid profile.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Both beans and rice provide fiber that supports digestive health.

items.title: Low glycemic impact
items.content: The combination of beans with whole‑grain rice helps stabilize blood sugar levels.

items.title: B‑vitamin content
items.content: Beans and rice contain thiamine, niacin and folate, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The dish supplies iron, magnesium and potassium, which aid muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans such as soy, lentils or chickpeas.

items.title: Anti‑nutrient content
items.content: Certain beans contain phytic acid and lectins that can reduce mineral absorption if not properly cooked.

items.title: High sodium in sauces
items.content: Prepared portions often come with salty sauces; monitor sodium intake.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Beans can cause gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive people, especially when not soaked or cooked thoroughly.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Beans and rice are served hot, typically in paper or plastic containers. Eat it as a standalone meal, add to salads, use as a filling for burritos, or as a side to meat dishes. Optional toppings include salsa, guacamole, shredded cheese or fresh cilantro.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat in a microwave or on a skillet. Frozen portions keep well for up to 2 months.
